meta.purpose: Measured editing rhythm of reference videos, used as the target spec for the montage planner. Our own output is measured with the same method so every iteration is comparable.
meta.tool: POST /analyze on the Railway render server (remotion/server/analyze.mjs); our own baseline measured locally with the same logic

method.cutDetection: ffmpeg select='gt(scene,THRESHOLD)' + showinfo; cuts closer than 0.15s merged
method.variability: standard deviation of shot durations divided by their mean — 0 means every shot is the same length
method.cutsWithAudioAccentPct: share of cuts where loudness right after the cut exceeds loudness 0.3s before it by >60% (SFX/impact hits landing on the cut)
method.cutsOnSpeechBoundaryPct: share of cuts falling within 0.4s of a caption cue start/end (cutting on the narration beat)
method.duckingRatioCaveat: ratio of loudness with no speech vs under speech. Unreliable when talkTimePct approaches 100, because the no-speech sample becomes tiny.

references.note: Illustrated/animated documentary (Alcatraz escape). Contains the clearest examples of the devices we lack: a black frame used as punctuation, a run of four ~1s archival headline cards, and eight consecutive 0.50s action inserts followed by a 34s hold.

observedShotContent.1: wide establishing — figure running on the shore (9.67s)
observedShotContent.6-9: four consecutive archival newspaper headline cards, ~1s each
observedShotContent.12-19: eight consecutive 0.50s action inserts — hand tool, vent shaft, drilling, corridor, yard, climbing a pipe, tunnel
observedShotContent.23: 34.3s uninterrupted hold immediately after the burst

references.note: The slowest of the five — median shot longer than ours. Proves the problem is not shot length but the absence of variation.
Narration pace closest to ours (117 wpm) and the most breathing room of the five.

atReferenceThreshold.note: At the same threshold used for all five references, the whole body of the video registers as ONE 42.9s shot. Our scene changes do not read as cuts because consecutive scenes share subject, location, framing and lighting.

atLoweredThreshold.note: Only when the detector is made far more sensitive do the scene boundaries appear — and they land on an 8-second grid.
atLoweredThreshold.gridEvidence: cuts at 8.0 / 16.0 / 24.0 / 32.5 — the 8s scene metronome, measured

defectsFound: Chapter card title truncated mid-word: rendered 'In the dimly lit Anci' — a sentence fragment is reaching the card instead of a title
Inconsistent framing: the final scene is letterboxed with black bands covering ~21% of frame height (measured at t=36s and t=42s), while scenes at t=3/12/20/27s fill the frame

styleCard.principle: Do not copy a speed — copy the structure. Reference medians span 1.3s to 9.1s (a 7x spread), so there is no single correct shot length. What all five share is extreme variation and a montage bound to the soundtrack.
rules: Shortest-to-longest ratio of at least 1:10 within one video
At least one burst of 3-8 short shots (0.4-1.2s) per minute
At least one held shot above 10s per minute
Never three consecutive shots of equal duration — except inside a deliberate rhythmic burst, where equal duration IS the effect
Bind picture to sound: 36-65% of cuts carry an audio accent in the references, 0% in ours
Punctuate with black frames of 0.3-1.5s before a reveal
Use typographic cards held ~1s in runs of 3-5 — as declared graphics, never photoreal fake newspaper scans, which would fabricate documents even when the underlying fact is true

acceptanceTargets.note: Re-measure our render with the same tool after each montage change.
acceptanceTargets.cutsDetectedAtThreshold: cuts must register at threshold 0.25, not only at 0.15
